section: Goods and Services Tax - structure, slabs, GST Council, IGST settlement, compensation cess
subsections: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a Central tax subsumed into the Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
accepted.x: Central Excise Duty was subsumed into GST. Basic Customs Duty, stamp duty and electricity duty continue outside GST.
accepted.tq: Identify the tax retained outside GST before selecting the subsumed tax.

accepted.s: Which of the following State taxes was subsumed into GST, subject to the stated exception?
o: Property Tax, except when imposed by local bodies
Electricity Duty, except when imposed by local bodies
Entertainment Tax, except when imposed by local bodies
Motor Vehicle Tax, except when imposed by local bodies
accepted.x: Entertainment Tax was subsumed into GST except when levied by local bodies. Electricity duty, property tax and motor vehicle tax remain outside GST.
accepted.tq: Focus on the exception attached to the correctly identified tax.

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of State taxes subsumed into GST?
o: Purchase Tax, Luxury Tax and Entry Tax
Stamp Duty, Electricity Duty and Property Tax
Motor Vehicle Tax, State Excise on Liquor and Stamp Duty
Basic Customs Duty, Purchase Tax and Electricity Duty
accepted.x: Purchase Tax, Luxury Tax and Entry Tax in all forms were subsumed into GST. The other groups contain taxes retained outside GST.
accepted.tq: Eliminate each group containing a retained tax.

accepted.s: The number of Central and State taxes subsumed into GST, as conventionally stated, is respectively:
accepted.x: The conventional classification identifies eight Central taxes and nine State taxes as subsumed into GST.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired numerical classification rather than counting only one category.

accepted.s: Which of the following concepts was dropped with the introduction of the GST framework?
accepted.x: The concept of declared goods of special importance was dropped under the GST framework. Destination-based taxation, input tax credit and taxation of supply are GST features.
accepted.tq: Test the discontinued concept against continuing GST mechanisms.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT retained outside GST?
accepted.x: Central Excise Duty was subsumed into GST. Basic Customs Duty, stamp duty and electricity duty are retained outside GST.
accepted.tq: Find the one item that does not belong among retained taxes.

accepted.s: A supplier pays tax on inputs and seeks to set it off against the tax payable on outward supplies. This facility is known as:
accepted.x: Input Tax Credit allows tax paid on inputs to be set off against output tax. It helps prevent cascading of taxes.
accepted.tq: Identify the mechanism from its practical business operation.

accepted.s: Under the Reverse Charge Mechanism in GST, the liability to pay tax is shifted from the:
accepted.x: Under reverse charge, the recipient, rather than the supplier, pays GST on specified supplies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the direction of liability by asking who actually remits the tax.

accepted.s: The anti-profiteering provision under Section 171 of the Central Goods and Services Tax framework is intended to ensure that:
o: The benefit of tax-rate reductions or input-tax credit reaches consumers
The supplier is exempt from GST when prices rise
All GST rates remain unchanged permanently
accepted.x: Section 171 requires the benefit of a rate reduction or input-tax credit to be passed on to consumers through commensurate reduction in prices.
accepted.tq: Link the statutory mechanism with its consumer-protection objective.

accepted.s: With effect from 1 October 2024, cases relating to anti-profiteering are handled by the:
o: Principal Bench of the GST Appellate Tribunal
accepted.x: From 1 October 2024, the Principal Bench of GSTAT handles anti-profiteering cases. The earlier institutional arrangements included the National Anti-Profiteering Authority and subsequently the CCI.
accepted.tq: Use the effective-date clue to identify the current adjudicatory body.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the electronic way bill:
1. It is an electronic document used for movement of goods.
2. It is required for goods valued above ₹50,000.
3. Its validity is one day for every 200 kilometres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: An e-way bill is an electronic document for movement of goods valued above ₹50,000, with validity of one day per 200 kilometres.
accepted.tq: Verify the document, value threshold and validity-period statements together.

accepted.s: Under the destination principle of GST, tax revenue primarily accrues to the State:
o: Where the goods or services are consumed
accepted.x: The destination principle assigns revenue to the State of consumption rather than the State of production or registration.
accepted.tq: Distinguish destination-based taxation from origin-based taxation.

accepted.s: A registered person opts for the composition scheme. Which one of the following combinations correctly describes the scheme?
o: ₹50 lakh goods turnover, ₹1.5 crore services turnover, 1% goods, 6% services and no ITC
₹1.5 crore goods turnover, ₹50 lakh services turnover, 6% goods, 1% services and full ITC
₹1.5 crore goods turnover, ₹50 lakh services turnover, 1% goods, 6% services and no ITC
₹50 lakh goods turnover, ₹1.5 crore services turnover, 6% goods, 1% services and full ITC
accepted.x: The composition scheme applies up to ₹1.5 crore for goods and ₹50 lakh for services, with rates of 1% for goods and 6% for services and no input tax credit.
accepted.tq: Match the turnover limits, rates and ITC consequence as one complete package.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the composition scheme is correct?
o: It does not allow input tax credit, although refunds may be allowed for an inverted duty structure.
It is available only to exporters making zero-rated supplies.
It replaces the destination principle with an origin principle.
It permits unrestricted input tax credit to the taxpayer.
accepted.x: A composition taxpayer cannot claim input tax credit. Refunds may nevertheless be permitted in relation to an inverted duty structure.
accepted.tq: Use the principal restriction to separate the composition scheme from the regular scheme.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes GSTIN?
o: A 16-digit number issued by the RBI
A 12-digit number for e-way bills only
A 10-digit identification number for direct taxpayers
accepted.x: GSTIN is a 15-digit Goods and Services Tax Identification Number. It is not a PAN, RBI number or e-way bill number.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical length to distinguish GSTIN from other identifiers.

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched with its GST compliance function?
o: E-invoicing — checking fake invoices; HSN/SAC — classification codes
E-invoicing — determining the State share of GST; HSN/SAC — fixing the repo rate
E-invoicing — replacing GSTIN; HSN/SAC — exempting all services
E-invoicing — collecting stamp duty; HSN/SAC — issuing passports
accepted.x: E-invoicing helps check fake invoices, while HSN and SAC are classification codes for goods and services respectively.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure compliance pair and reject unrelated administrative functions.

accepted.s: For low-risk applicants, automated GST registration is to be completed within:
accepted.x: Automated registration for low-risk applicants is completed within three working days.
accepted.tq: Recall the prescribed time limit and distinguish working days from calendar periods.

accepted.s: Revenue Neutral Rate (RNR) in the context of GST refers to a rate that:
o: Keeps revenue equal to the level prevailing before GST
Maximises tax revenue irrespective of the pre-GST position
accepted.x: RNR is the rate designed to keep revenue at the pre-GST level. The concept was associated with the Arvind Subramanian Committee in 2015.
accepted.tq: Match the technical term with its precise revenue objective.

accepted.s: The Revenue Neutral Rate in relation to GST was associated with the committee headed by:
accepted.x: The Revenue Neutral Rate was associated with the Arvind Subramanian Committee, constituted in 2015 for this purpose.
accepted.tq: Use the committee-chairperson association rather than confusing it with other fiscal committees.

accepted.s: Which of the following is constitutionally within the GST framework but is to be levied under GST only from a date recommended by the GST Council?
accepted.x: The Constitution permits petroleum products to be brought under GST from a date recommended by the GST Council. Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is excluded by the Constitution itself.
accepted.tq: Separate constitutional inclusion with deferred levy from constitutional exclusion.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: Which one of the following is constitutionally excluded from GST rather than merely awaiting a notified date for levy?
accepted.x: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is constitutionally excluded from GST. The listed petroleum products are constitutionally within GST but have not been brought under it for levy.
accepted.tq: Compare the constitutional treatment of liquor with petroleum products.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five petroleum products kept outside the current levy of GST?
accepted.x: The five petroleum products are crude oil, petrol or motor spirit, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel. Lubricating oil is not included in that specified list.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete five-item list and identify the outsider.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s:
Consider the following items:
1. Electricity supply
2. Real estate transactions subject to stamp duty
3. Alcoholic liquor for human consumption
4. Aviation turbine fuel
Which of the above are outside the current GST levy?
accepted.x: Electricity, real estate transactions subject to stamp duty, alcoholic liquor for human consumption and aviation turbine fuel are outside the current GST levy.
accepted.tq: Treat each item independently and select the complete set of excluded items.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes zero-rated supplies from nil-rated supplies under GST?
o: Nil-rated supplies are taxable at the standard rate, whereas zero-rated supplies are exempt by notification.
Zero-rated supplies include exports and SEZ supplies with full ITC refund; nil-rated supplies do not allow ITC.
Zero-rated supplies carry a 0% rate and nil-rated supplies allow full ITC refund.
Both categories are identical because neither permits ITC.
accepted.x: Exports and supplies to SEZs are zero-rated and permit full input tax credit refund. Nil-rated supplies attract a zero rate and do not permit ITC.
accepted.tq: Compare both the type of supply and the input-tax-credit consequence.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: A supply is specifically exempted from GST by notification. Which one of the following follows from this classification?
o: It is automatically zero-rated and full ITC must be refunded.
It is taxed at the highest GST slab.
It is an exempt supply and input tax credit is unavailable.
It can be treated as an export irrespective of destination.
accepted.x: An exempt supply is notified as being outside tax and does not qualify for input tax credit. Exemption is distinct from zero-rating.
accepted.tq: Apply the ITC consequence to distinguish exempt from zero-rated supplies.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Nil-rated — 0% rate; exempt — notified out of tax; zero-rated — exports and SEZ supplies
Nil-rated — full ITC refund; exempt — exports; zero-rated — no ITC
Nil-rated — only petroleum supplies; exempt — only liquor; zero-rated — only domestic supplies
Nil-rated — stamp duty; exempt — customs duty; zero-rated — electricity duty
accepted.x: Nil-rated supplies attract a zero rate, exempt supplies are notified out of tax, and zero-rated supplies include exports and SEZ supplies with full ITC refund.
accepted.tq: Match each term with its exact legal and ITC consequence.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: Under the GST 2.0 changes referred to in the current tax structure, which of the following is exempted?
o: All motor vehicle insurance premiums without exception
Individual life and health insurance premiums
accepted.x: GST 2.0 provides exemption for individual life and health insurance premiums. The exemption is not stated as a blanket exemption for every insurance service.
accepted.tq: Avoid extending a specific exemption into an unsupported blanket exemption.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: Under the GST 2.0 changes, rare-disease medicines are treated as:
o: Taxable at the highest GST rate
Outside GST but subject to stamp duty
accepted.x: Rare-disease medicines are fully exempt under the stated GST 2.0 changes.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise tax treatment rather than confusing exemption with zero-rating.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between GST and input tax credit for non-taxable or exempt supplies?
o: ITC is compulsory even when no GST is charged.
ITC is available only on supplies subject to stamp duty.
ITC is available on every exempt and non-taxable supply.
ITC is not available on exempt or non-taxable supplies.
accepted.x: Input tax credit is not available on exempt or non-taxable supplies. Zero-rated supplies are different because they permit full ITC refund.
accepted.tq: Use the ITC rule to separate exempt and non-taxable supplies from zero-rated supplies.
accepted.sec: Items outside GST; exempt vs nil vs zero-rated
